body: W3 design question before final candidate (no edit): PseudonymizationDetector.checked is necessarily public so interview/other modules can supply a span finder. Therefore an external caller can create permissive/v1 with config permissive/v1, return exactly the caller's map spans on source and zero on destination, obtain a detectorCertified PseudonymizedText, and RemotePolicy.evaluate authorizes it because it checks only the private certification bit + policy/provider/model/purpose. The receipts make this fully auditable, but do not establish that the policy trusts that detector/configuration. Is that provenance-only trust boundary intentional? If not, I recommend a typed DetectorPolicyIdentity(detectorId, configurationDigest: ReceiptDigest.Keyed) allowlist on RemotePolicy, checked against both retained receipts; ID alone is insufficient because IDs are public opaque IDs. This is a design expansion, so I am holding code pending your disposition.
